$comment: Triage decision table used by `node security/make-baseline.mjs` to GENERATE security/baseline.json (one entry per finding fingerprint). First matching decision wins. Every decision is a PROPOSAL by the implementing agent until an independent reviewer approves it. Narrow by design: a decision never matches vendored dependencies, and any NEW finding (different fingerprint) is un-triaged again. High/critical findings are never suppressed by a scope-wide wildcard: each is listed with its own fingerprint and reason.

decisions.reason: SET statement_timeout cannot take a bind parameter; the interpolated value is a number produced by Math.floor/Math.max or an already-validated integer from server config, never user input.

Interpolated fragments are constants: a ternary between two fixed column names, or the WHERE fragment of revokeUserVerifications() which is now typed as a union of three literal strings; every value is a bind parameter.
decisions.requiredFix: none (the helper's `where` parameter was narrowed to a literal union in this change)

decisions.reason: Operator/dev tooling (benchmark, backup rehearsal) builds CREATE/DROP DATABASE statements from names it generates itself (forge_bench_<n>_<pid>); DDL identifiers cannot be bind parameters and no external input reaches them.

Third-party and first-party actions are referenced by mutable tag (e.g. actions/checkout@v4) rather than a full commit SHA, so a compromised or force-moved tag would run in CI with the job's token. Real supply-chain hardening gap; not exploitable by a PR author, hence medium.
decisions.requiredFix: Pin every `uses:` to a full commit SHA (keep the tag in a comment) and let Dependabot/Renovate bump them; tracked as follow-up outside this tooling change.

decisions.reason: ForgeProtocolRevenueSplitter._send only pays the fixed treasuryRecipient (claimTreasury, msg.sender-checked) or the recipient of releaseNonRevenue; it is private, called after state updates, under nonReentrant, with the result checked. 'Arbitrary' is the scanner's view of an address parameter.

pullRevenue is nonReentrant and calls only the canonical PonsV2FeeEscrow (claim/claimToken); the ETH leg re-enters only receive(), which is gated by the _pullingNative flag. Amounts are measured from the balance delta, not trusted from return values; the escrow return values are intentionally ignored. Covered by the splitter invariant suite (conservation, no over-pull) and the W05 attestor tests.

`received == 0` / `amount == 0` are sentinel checks on locally computed values (balance delta, requested amount) that revert with NothingReceived or select the 'all headroom' mode; they are not attacker-steerable balance equality.

Two deliberate low-level calls: the checked ETH transfer in _send, and the ArbSys staticcall in _evidenceView whose result length/success is validated (falls back to the EVM opcodes only when ArbSys does not answer). Both are covered by tests (W05EmergencyRevocation/ForgeRevenueSplitter test_H2_*).

The 'external calls' preceding the state writes are view reads (escrow balanceOf, factory/token policy getters) in authorizeEligibleRevenue/setAssetApproved (owner-only), or the guarded escrow claim inside the nonReentrant pullRevenue whose state writes ARE the reentrancy guard (_pullingNative).
_matured(pending*) receives a memory COPY only to read effectiveAt/expiresAt/newRecipient; the storage struct is cleared with `delete pending*` afterwards. No storage array is edited through memory.

feeEscrow.claim/claimToken return values are intentionally ignored: pullRevenue accounts for what actually arrived via the balance delta (NothingReceived on zero) and bounds it by the attested ceiling.

requireAuthorizedLaunchCall declares the decoded launch parameters up front and assigns every one by abi.decode tuple destructuring in each non-reverting branch (unknown selectors revert UnknownLaunchEntry).
setEligibilityAuthority(address(0)) is the deliberate on-chain kill switch that disables all launches/bindings (authority matrix: emergency control). A zero check would remove the incident control.
Same as missing-zero-check: address(0) authority is the intended kill-switch state, only the owner can set it, and the change is monitored (EligibilityAuthorityUpdated).
Constructor of the PONS-derived factory: the flagged external call is a view (positionManager_.poolManager()) wiring check before immutables are set; no external party can re-enter a constructor.

_exemptFromSnipeTax calls the curve once per exemption entry; the array is supplied by the launching creator for their own launch and is bounded by gas/launch economics; behaviour is inherited from PONS and covered by W01 regression tests.

Informational/low: deadline and expiry checks intentionally use block.timestamp (minutes-to-days windows); one audited EIP-712 assembly block; complexity of the signature-verification paths is covered by the M-ELIG adversarial suite; local names shadow OZ helper names harmlessly.

Timelocks (3 days) and attestation deadlines intentionally use block.timestamp; validator skew of seconds is immaterial. Complexity is in the attestation/pull validation path, covered by the splitter unit, invariant and W05 compromised-attestor suites.

Owner-gated functions are the documented governance model; each is classified in the 103-function authority matrix (docs/W05-AUTHORITY-MATRIX.md), owner is a Safe + timelock in the target deployment, standing owner powers F-03/F-04/W05-03 are disclosed and routed to external review C03.
decisions.requiredFix: external review C03; no code change

decisions.reason: Style/gas-level notes: the compiler is pinned to 0.8.35 by foundry.toml (profile forge) regardless of the ^ pragma, PUSH0 is intended for the cancun target, loops that revert validate caller-supplied arrays, and none changes fund flow. Revisit during the external audit.

Unmodified inherited PONS code (byte-identical to the deploy-time tree pinned in provenance/). Changing it would invalidate the deployed-source evidence, so it cannot be patched here. Not independently exploit-triaged by Forge; deferred to the external audit (C01) and PONS Labs. See docs/SECURITY-REVIEW.md.
decisions.requiredFix: none in this repository; external audit C01
